The image presents a visually appealing apple pie with a lattice crust, resting on a white plate. A slice has been neatly removed, revealing the filling. Red and green apples are arranged around the pie, with apples that have been peeled and cut into slices, likely indicating their use in the pie.

Apples were not commonly used in early pie recipes due to their lack of sweetness, a quality that developed in Europe only in the early 19th century. Therefore, very early pies typically contained meat, and fruit pies were sweetened with sugar, which was considered a luxury product. Sugar became more affordable to the general population around the mid-18th century.

The pie is displayed on a surface that resembles marble, characterized by its white color with black speckles, creating a sophisticated backdrop for the arrangement.
